# Leveling reference

The level and XP components every leveling unit and XP-giving enemy carries, and the XP curve asset. For how to use it, see [Leveling](../modules/leveling.md).

## VtUnitLevel

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Leveling → VtUnitLevel**.

Per-unit level and XP tracker. Added automatically when the unit definition has an `VtUnitDefinition.xpCurve`; add it yourself on a prefab-authored unit. Units that never level (most NPCs) go without it.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Curve (`curve`) | [VtXpCurveDefinition](#vtxpcurvedefinition) | None |  | XP curve this unit progresses on. Filled from the unit definition's XP Curve when the unit spawns; assign it here for prefab-authored units. |
| Starting Level (`startingLevel`) | `int` | 1 | ≥ 1 | Starting level for fresh units. Most games start at 1; some prologues open at higher levels (5, 10) to skip onboarding XP. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `int Level { get; }` | The unit's current level. Initialized to `startingLevel` on first `Awake`; mutated by `AddXp` / `SetLevel`. |
| `int CurrentXp { get; }` | Accumulated XP since the last level-up. Always less than the XP needed for the next level (excess is consumed by leveling). |
| `int XpToNextLevel { get; }` | XP needed to advance from `Level` to the next level. 0 when the unit is at the curve's max level. |
| `bool IsMaxLevel { get; }` | True when the unit has reached the curve's `maxLevel` and further XP gains are dropped. |
| `event Action<int, int> OnLeveledUp` | Fires once after every `AddXp` call that produces at least one level-up. Args: (oldLevel, newLevel). For multi-level jumps fires once with the full old → new range; subscribe and walk `(oldLevel + 1)..newLevel` if you need per-level work. |
| `event Action<int, int, int> OnXpChanged` | Fires after any mutation to `CurrentXp` (gain or reset), AFTER any level-ups have been applied. Args: (currentLevel, currentXp, xpToNext). Use for XP-bar UI. |
| `void Initialize()` | Seed `Level` from `startingLevel` the first time it's called; subsequent calls are no-ops. Mid-run re-seeds (re-applying the same definition on respawn, swapping definitions) preserve the unit's current level rather than resetting to 1. |
| `void SeedFromDefinitionStartingLevel(int startingLevelFromDef)` | Apply a unit definition's starting level. The first call sets the level to `startingLevelFromDef`; later calls only update `startingLevel`, so respawns and definition swaps keep the current level. |
| `void AddXp(int amount)` | Credit experience from gameplay (kills, quest turn-ins). Scales `amount` by 1 plus the unit's XP gain multiplier stat (`VtCoreStats.xpGainMultiplier`), then levels up as often as the total allows, firing `OnLeveledUp` once if any level was crossed. Authority-gated. Negative or zero amounts no-op. |
| `void AddXp(int amount, bool applyGainMultiplier)` | Credit experience with explicit control over the gain multiplier. Pass `applyGainMultiplier: false` for save-game restore, admin commands, or any flow that must credit exactly `amount`. Otherwise identical to `AddXp`. |
| `void SetLevel(int level)` | Force-set the unit's level. Resets `CurrentXp` to 0. Authority-gated. Used by save-game restore, admin commands, mentor systems. Clamps to `[1, curve.maxLevel]`. |
| `void Reset()` | Wipe XP back to 0 but keep current level. Authority-gated. |
| `void RemoveXp(int amount)` | Take `amount` XP away within the current level. Never drops a level; stops at zero. A death penalty uses this. |
| `void ApplyLevelFromNet(int level, int xp)` | Net-replication entry point. Replaces both fields with the authoritative snapshot. Bypasses the authority gate. Fires `OnLeveledUp` if the level changed; always fires `OnXpChanged`. |

## VtXpAwarder

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Leveling → VtXpAwarder**.

Awards `xpAward` when this unit dies: the killer, and party members who share the credit, split it through their `VtUnitLevel`. Added automatically when the unit definition sets an XP award.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Xp Award (`xpAward`) | `int` | 0 | ≥ 0 | XP credited to the killer on this unit's death. 0 = no XP awarded (equivalent to not having the awarder attached). Filled from the unit definition's XP Award when the unit spawns; set it here for prefab-authored mobs. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `void Initialize()` | Caches the sibling `VtUnitStats` reference and subscribes to `VtUnitStats.OnDied`. Idempotent — safe to call any number of times. |

## VtXpCurveDefinition

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → Leveling → XP Curve**.

Authored XP-to-next-level curve. Designer drops in the per-level XP thresholds; the level component looks up "how much XP does the next level cost" and "what level am I at given a total XP value."

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Id (`id`) | `string` | Empty |  | Stable id used in logs and as a stable serialization key. Convention: 'curve.<flavor>' (e.g. 'curve.standard', 'curve.fast', 'curve.slow'). Required. |
| Display Name (`displayName`) | `string` | Empty |  | Designer-facing name. Shown in inspector dropdowns. |
| Description (`description`) | `string` | Empty |  | Designer-facing description (e.g. 'Standard pacing — capped at 60 with 1.1x extrapolation past the array'). |
| Max Level (`maxLevel`) | `int` | 60 | ≥ 1 | Maximum level reachable on this curve. AddXp on a unit at maxLevel drops the excess silently. Default 60 — typical for most games. |
| Xp To Next Level (`xpToNextLevel`) | `int`[] | Empty |  | Per-level XP thresholds. Index 0 = XP to go from level 1 → 2. Index 1 = XP to go from level 2 → 3. Etc. Author 10–60 explicit values; extrapolation handles anything past the array (see extrapolatePercent). |
| Extrapolate Percent (`extrapolatePercent`) | `float` | 0.1 | 0 to 5 | When current level exceeds the array length, the threshold extrapolates as lastThreshold × (1 + extrapolatePercent × levelsPastArray). 0 = hard-cap at the array's last entry. 0.1 = each level past the array costs 10% more than the previous. Used to soft-cap progression past the explicit values. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `int GetXpToNextLevel(int currentLevel)` | XP required to advance from `currentLevel` to `currentLevel + 1`. Returns 0 when the unit is already at `maxLevel` (no further progression possible). |
